title: graphql
text:
from datetime import datetime, timezone, timedelta
from fastcore.test import *
from pyskills import xdir, doc
Cloudflare exposes R2 storage and operations, Workers, KV, D1, DNS, HTTP, and firewall analytics exclusively through its GraphQL Analytics API.
CfGql wraps fastspec’s GraphQL client with Cloudflare’s distilled schema and the same CLOUDFLARE_* credentials as CloudflareApi. Explore datasets offline with xdir, doc, and gql.t, chain attributes with keyword arguments to build field-checked queries, or pass raw GraphQL text directly.

CfGql
CfGql configures GqlClient with Cloudflare’s GraphQL endpoint, the bundled schema, and CLOUDFLARE_* authentication. account() and zone() build filtered viewer.accounts and viewer.zones fragments.

title: graphql
text:
Discovery and R2 analytics
Use xdir and doc to inspect available datasets and filter arguments offline without sending a request:

api_key = os.getenv('CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY')
gql = CfGql(api_key=api_key) if api_key else CfGql()
xdir(gql.account(), 'r2')


doc(gql.account().r2StorageAdaptiveGroups)

Inspect filter input objects and orderBy enums with gql.t:

doc(gql.t.AccountR2StorageAdaptiveGroupsOrderBy)

Query per-bucket R2 storage usage over the last two days:

if api_key and gql.account_id:
    since = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=2)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
    f = gql.account().r2StorageAdaptiveGroups(filter={'date_geq': since}, limit=20, orderBy=['max_payloadSize_DESC'])
    rows = (await f('dimensions { bucketName } max { payloadSize objectCount }'))[0]
    assert isinstance(rows, (list, L))
    [(r.dimensions.bucketName, r.max.payloadSize, r.max.objectCount) for r in rows]

title: FastCF
text:
fastcflare provides async Python access to Cloudflare’s REST (CloudflareApi) and GraphQL Analytics (CfGql) APIs from bundled schemas. Browse operations, manage zones and DNS records, create scoped zone and R2 S3 tokens, and query R2, Workers, DNS, and HTTP analytics.
from fastcore.utils import *
from fastcflare import *

title: FastCF
text:
Quickstart

from fastcflare import *


ucf = CloudflareApi()
(await ucf.verify()).result.status

'active'



(await ucf.zones.list()).result[0].name

'aaa.as'



Create a token
Create a token with Zone Read and DNS Write permissions for one domain. Replace xxx with the domain name. The client used to create it must have permission to create tokens:
doms = ['xxx']
pnms = ('Zone Read', 'DNS Write')
tok = await ucf.create_token(doms, pnms, 'domain mgt')
dns_token = tok.result.value
Store the token securely. For APIs that accept a Global API Key, construct the client with CloudflareApi(api_key=os.environ['CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY']) (reading CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID from the environment) instead. For R2 S3 credentials, use await gcf.create_r2_token('name', buckets='my-bucket').
Use the new token to list DNS records, create a test A record, and delete that record. This changes DNS records in an existing zone; it does not create or delete the domain:
domnm = 'xxx'
zones = (await ucf.zones.list(name=domnm)).result
zid_sp = zones[0].id

dcf = CloudflareApi(token=dns_token)
print((await dcf.zones.dns_records.list(zone_id=zid_sp)).result[:3])
rec = await dcf.zones.dns_records.post(zid_sp, type='A', name='test-delete-me.xxx', content='192.0.2.1', ttl=1)
print(rec.result.id, rec.result.name)
print((await dcf.zones.dns_records.delete(zid_sp, rec.result.id)).result.id)

title: FastCF
text:
Intro to Account Tokens
Account-owned API tokens belong to an account and act as service principals with their own permissions. They support CI/CD and service integrations that need to keep working after the creating user leaves the organization. The API endpoint is /accounts/{id}/tokens.

Creating Account Tokens
Cloudflare requires Super Administrator permission to create or update account-owned tokens. The creation endpoint accepts an API token with Account API Tokens Write. The following example uses the official Cloudflare Python SDK with token authentication:
from cloudflare import Cloudflare
cf = Cloudflare(api_token=your_cf_token)
accts = cf.accounts.list()
acct_id = next(iter(accts)).id
Look up permission groups available to the account:
groups = list(cf.accounts.tokens.permission_groups.list(account_id=acct_id))
{g.name: g.id for g in groups if 'dns' in g.name.lower() or 'zone' in g.name.lower()}
For account-owned tokens, nest zone resources under the account resource. This example grants Zone Read and DNS Write across its zones:
tok = cf.accounts.tokens.create(account_id=acct_id, name="dns-all-zones", policies=[{
    "effect": "allow",
    "resources": {f"com.cloudflare.api.account.{acct_id}": {"com.cloudflare.api.account.zone.*": "*"}},
    "permission_groups": [{"id": g.id} for g in groups if g.name in ('Zone Read', 'DNS Write')]
}])
dns_tok = tok.value  # Store securely; the value is only returned at creation
A zone resource without the enclosing account, such as {"com.cloudflare.api.account.zone.*": "*"}, fails with: “Must specify a zone for account owned tokens, or nest zone under specific account resource”. Keep the nested format even when granting access to all zones.

Development
The REST and GraphQL surfaces ship as compact specs in cf_spec.py and gql_spec.py. Refresh both with tools/build.py, then review the diff: REST op names can shift when Cloudflare updates its OpenAPI schema.

title: FastCF
text:
CloudflareApi
Cloudflare’s operationIds are machine artifacts (zones-get vs zones-0-get — the -0- is a generator’s dedup counter), so rather than cleaning them up we name every op mechanically from its verb and path: the group is the path’s non-parameter segments, nested (zones.dns_records), and the method is the HTTP verb — except that when a group has both a collection GET and a single-item GET they become list and get. Two fixups keep the whole surface collision-free: sibling paths differing only by an interior parameter gain a _by_<param> suffix, and an action segment that would shadow an op folds into its parent as <segment>_<verb>. So GET /zones is zones.list, GET /zones/{zone_id} is zones.get, and GET /user/tokens/verify is user.tokens.verify.get — a user who knows the URL knows the call.


source

cf_names
def cf_names(
    spec
):
Map each op’s canonical (verb, snaked-segments) key to (group_segments, op_name), collision-free across the surface




source

cf_group_func
def cf_group_func(
    names
):
A fastspec group_func looking up precomputed names by canonical verb+path


The parsed surface ships with the package as cf_spec.py, fastspec’s compact form (SpecParser.save): 2.6MB instead of the 8MB raw schema, loaded in ~30ms instead of a ~0.3s parse, with the naming machinery above running only at regeneration time. build_spec refreshes it from Cloudflare’s published schema; op names can shift when the spec changes, so review that diff before shipping it.


source

build_spec
def build_spec(
    nm:str='fastcflare/cf_spec.py',
    url:str='https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cloudflare/api-schemas/main/openapi.json'
):
Regenerate the compact spec module cf_spec.py from Cloudflare’s OpenAPI schema.



cli = OpenAPIClient(_cf_spec(), headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {tok}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
sorted(cli.groups)

['accounts',
 'certificates',
 'internal',
 'ips',
 'live',
 'memberships',
 'organizations',
 'radar',
 'ready',
 'signed_url',
 'system',
 'tenants',
 'user',
 'users',
 'zones']


The naming is only trustworthy if it can never silently collide — OpGroup exposes ops with setattr, so a duplicate name would shadow its sibling (exactly the bug this design replaces). This walk asserts the built tree is clean: within every group, op names are unique (duplicates allowed only for the same endpoint spelled two ways in the spec) and no op shares a name with a subgroup.

def _surface_ok(g):
    nms = [o.name for o in g.ops]
    for n,c in Counter(nms).items():
        if c>1: assert len({tuple(snake(s) for s in o.op_spec.path.strip('/').split('/')) for o in g.ops if o.name==n})==1, f'dup op {g.name}.{n}'
    assert not set(nms)&set(g.subgroups), f'op/subgroup shadow in {g.name}: {set(nms)&set(g.subgroups)}'
    for sg in g.subgroups.values(): _surface_ok(sg)

for grp in cli.groups.values(): _surface_ok(grp)
len(cli.groups), len(cli.groups['zones'].subgroups)

(15, 60)

title: FastCF
text:
R2 tokens and S3 credentials
Cloudflare R2 S3 credentials derive directly from an R2 API token: access_key_id is the token ID and secret_access_key is the SHA-256 hex digest of the token value. create_r2_token creates either an account-owned service token (default) or a user token, scoped to specific buckets or the whole account, and returns both the API response and derived S3 credentials.


source

r2_s3_creds
def r2_s3_creds(
    token_id:str, # Cloudflare API token ID (becomes `access_key_id`)
    token_value:str, # Cloudflare API token secret value (SHA-256 hex becomes `secret_access_key`)
    account_id:str=None, # Account ID; defaults to `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`
    jurisdiction:str='default', # R2 jurisdiction (`'default'`, `'eu'`, `'fedramp'`)
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Derive S3-compatible R2 credentials (access_key_id, secret_access_key, endpoint, region) from a Cloudflare R2 API token.


r2_s3_creds derives S3 credentials offline from any existing token pair:

creds = r2_s3_creds('tok-id', 'tok-val', account_id='acct123')
assert len(creds.secret_access_key) == 64 and creds.endpoint == 'https://acct123.r2.cloudflarestorage.com'
creds.endpoint, creds.region



source

CloudflareApi.create_r2_token
async def create_r2_token(
    name:str, # Name for the new R2 token
    buckets:NoneType=None, # Bucket name or iterable of bucket names; None grants account-wide R2 access
    write:bool=True, # Grant read/write access (False for read-only)
    account_id:str=None, # Account ID; defaults to `self.account_id`
    account_token:bool=True, # Create an account-owned service token (False for a user-owned token)
    jurisdiction:str='default', # R2 jurisdiction for bucket-scoped resources (`'default'`, `'eu'`, `'fedramp'`)
    expires_on:str=None, # Optional RFC3339 expiration timestamp
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Create a Cloudflare R2 API token and return both the API response (token) and derived S3 credentials (s3).


Global API key authentication fills email and account_id from CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID:

if api_key and email and acctid:
    gcf = CloudflareApi(api_key=api_key)
    assert (await gcf.verify()).success


if api_key and email and acctid:
    r2 = await gcf.create_r2_token('fastcflare-r2-test-token', buckets='fastcflare-test-bucket', write=False)
    try:
        assert r2.token.success and len(r2.s3.secret_access_key) == 64
        r2_cf = CloudflareApi(token=r2.token.result.value, account_token=True)
        assert (await r2_cf.verify()).result.status == 'active'
    finally: assert (await gcf.accounts.tokens.delete(acctid, r2.token.result.id)).success
    r2.s3.endpoint, r2.s3.region
